title: Find in a Rotated List
statement:
A list of **different** numbers was sorted from smallest to largest and then **rotated**: it was cut at some position and the two parts were swapped, so `[0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7]` can become `[4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1, 2]`. (It may also be left unrotated.)

Return the **index** of `target` in `nums`, or `-1` if it is not there.
constraints: nums is a sorted list that was rotated by some amount

hints.nudge: In a rotated sorted list, when you cut at the middle, at least one half is still properly sorted. Which one?
hints.pattern: Binary search where you first decide which half is sorted, then check whether the target lies in that half.
hints.pseudocode:
lo = 0; hi = n-1
while lo <= hi:
  mid = (lo + hi) / 2; if nums[mid] == target: return mid
  if nums[lo] <= nums[mid]:   // left half sorted
    if nums[lo] <= target < nums[mid]: hi = mid - 1 else: lo = mid + 1
  else:                       // right half sorted
    if nums[mid] < target <= nums[hi]: lo = mid + 1 else: hi = mid - 1
return -1
hints.walkthrough: A linear scan is O(n). To keep O(log n), notice that after splitting at mid, one of the two halves has no rotation point inside it, so it is plainly sorted: you can tell which by comparing nums[lo] with nums[mid]. Check whether the target falls inside the range of the sorted half. If it does, search that half; if it does not, it can only be in the other half. Repeat. Each step halves the range.
